title: California's 'Find Your Ally' Offers Free Immigration Legal Aid to 2.1 Million College Students
excerpt: The first state-funded program of its kind provides free legal help to all California community college students and their families, with demand nearly doubling as immigration enforcement intensifies.
body:
• California's Find Your Ally program offers free immigration legal assistance to all 2.1 million students across 116 community colleges, regardless of immigration status or enrollment type.
  • Funded at $10 million annually by the state, the program has served over 30,000 students since its 2019 launch and nearly doubled its annual intake in the most recent year.
  • Services include DACA renewal fee coverage, naturalization assistance, advance parole applications, family petitions, and guidance for mixed-status households.
  • All case information is protected by attorney-client privilege, with personal data scrubbed from the system within 48 hours of scheduling a consultation.

As immigration enforcement actions intensify across the United States, a California program is providing a critical safety net for college students navigating the complex immigration system — entirely free of charge.

Find Your Ally, operated through the Higher Education Legal Services Project, connects every student enrolled in California's 116 community colleges with free immigration legal assistance. The program is open to all students — full-time, part-time, credit, noncredit, dual enrollment, and adult education — as well as campus faculty and staff, regardless of their immigration status.

A First-of-Its-Kind State Investment

California community colleges serve over 2.1 million students, making it the largest higher education system in the United States. An estimated 50,000 to 70,000 of these students are undocumented, according to California Dream Act and in-state tuition application data.

https://x.com/nickshirleyy/status/2094163376700100853

Funded entirely by the state at roughly $10 million annually, the program remains insulated from federal government shutdowns and California's budget pressures. Since its launch in 2019 through a partnership between the Foundation for California Community Colleges and the California Department of Social Services, Find Your Ally has served more than 30,000 students and nearly doubled its previous yearly average in the most recent period.

"We do not ask for a lot of information. Most of it is contact information. There are a number of firewalls, and we scrub the system within 48 hours of scheduling their consultation."

— Alonso Garcia, Senior Manager of Equity, Foundation for California Community Colleges

Services Tailored to Immigrant Families

The range of legal services goes well beyond basic consultations. Students and their families can access help with Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals (DACA) renewal and filing fees, naturalization applications, advance parole filings, family petitions, and guidance for mixed-status households navigating changing immigration laws.

The program also assists with attending or funding immigration-related appointments, including doctor's visits required for certain filings. Crucially, program access continues even after a student or staff member leaves the community college system, with all case information protected under attorney-client privilege.

To access services, individuals can visit findyourally.com, enter their zip code or college of attendance, and be connected to the immigration attorney supporting that campus within minutes.

Growing Demand Amid Enforcement Surge

The program's growth comes against a backdrop of significantly heightened immigration enforcement under the Trump administration, which has expanded deportation operations, accelerated immigration court proceedings through mass hearings, and moved to restrict access to benefits for undocumented immigrants.

Immigration attorneys and advocacy groups have noted that the enforcement climate has driven many immigrant families to seek legal counsel, particularly around DACA renewals, work authorization, and advance parole — all services that Find Your Ally provides at no cost.

Relevance for the Indian Diaspora

For Indian students and families in California's community college system — many of whom hold H-4 dependent visas, are DACA recipients, or are navigating work authorization challenges — the program offers a direct resource. Indian immigrants represent a significant share of DACA applicants, and many face complex family-based petition processes that benefit from professional legal guidance.

California is home to one of the largest Indian-American populations in the country, with significant concentrations in the Bay Area, Los Angeles, and the Central Valley — all regions served by community colleges participating in the program.

What's Next

With demand trending sharply upward and the immigration enforcement landscape unlikely to ease, the program's organizers say they are working to expand outreach and ensure students are aware that services are available, free, and confidential. The program's model has drawn attention from other states considering similar initiatives, though none have yet replicated California's fully state-funded approach.
